What It Does

More than a polymer. It's what keeps the bore working.

Carry Flow is a partially hydrolysed polyacrylamide (PHPA) polymer — the same chemistry trusted on major HDD crossings, large-diameter waterbores, and bored piles throughout Australasia.

Unlike straight bentonite, Carry Flow encapsulates clay particles to prevent them swelling and sticking to tooling, while simultaneously building the viscosity needed to carry cuttings to surface. The result is a cleaner bore, less bit balling, and smoother pull-back.

It works as a standalone product in polymer-only systems, or as a critical additive in bentonite blends — giving you control over cuttings transport regardless of what the ground throws at you.

  • Clay encapsulation

    PHPA chains coat clay particles, preventing hydration and stopping reactive clays from swelling into the bore.

  • Cuttings transport

    Builds viscosity and gel strength to suspend and carry rock, sand, and clay cuttings to surface efficiently.

  • Bore wall stabilisation

    Forms a thin, flexible filter cake that supports the bore wall without blocking fluid circulation.

  • Lubricates tooling

    Reduces drag on the drill string and reaming tools, lowering torque and extending bit life.

Applications

Where Carry Flow works

From HDD crossings to large-diameter waterbores and bored piles, Carry Flow appears in more Blick fluid programs than any other single product.

Horizontal Directional Drilling

Used in every HDD fluid program from sticky clay to rock and gravel. Carries cuttings in both pilot and ream passes and helps pull-back go smoothly by lubricating the product pipe.

Sticky clay Sand & gravel Rock Large diameter

Waterwell Drilling

Essential in WA-style sand waterbores and reactive clay conditions. Provides the cuttings-carrying capacity and clay inhibition needed for deep, large-diameter holes without over-thickening the fluid.

Sand Reactive clay WA waterbores

Bored Piling

In PHPA piling systems, Carry Flow is used in combination with Swell Stop Dry and Filter High to create a stable polymer fluid that maintains pile shape from excavation through to concrete pour.

PHPA system Bored piles
Technical Data

Dosage & mixing

Carry Flow is added to the mix water after the initial water conditioning step (Soda Ash). Always mix into fresh, pH-adjusted water — never add to contaminated or heavily weighted fluid without consulting Blick.

Product type Liquid polymer (PHPA)
Dosage range 2–5 L per 1,000 L fluid
Mixing order After Soda Ash; before additives
Appearance Clear to pale amber liquid
Compatibility Bentonite, polymer, foam systems
Storage Cool, dry; protect from freezing
SDS / TDS Available from Blick
Standard Dosage
2–5
Litres per 1,000 L of fluid
HDD (clay, sand, rock) 2–5 L/1000L
Waterwell (sand) 2–5 L/1000L
Waterwell (reactive clay) 2–5 L/1000L
Piling (PHPA system) 2–5 L/1000L

Dosage rates are indicative. Ground conditions, bore diameter, and depth affect optimal concentration. Contact Blick for project-specific recommendations.

Mixing Guide

Adding Carry Flow to the mix

Mixing order matters. Adding products in the wrong sequence can cause flocculation, reduce performance, and waste product. Carry Flow always follows water conditioning — never add it to hard water or acidic pH.

Key rule: Always add Soda Ash to condition the water first. Once pH is 8.5–9.5, add Carry Flow and allow to fully hydrate (5–10 minutes circulation) before adding other products.
1
Soda Ash
Add to tank water. Adjust pH to 8.5–9.5. Circulate 5 min.
2
Carry Flow
Add slowly while circulating. Circulate 5–10 min until fully hydrated.
3
Bentonite (if required)
Add to polymer-conditioned water. Carry Flow improves bentonite hydration.
4
Inhibitors & additives
Clay Control, Swell Stop, Detergent, Biocide 75, Torque Down as required.
5
Check & drill
Check viscosity (Marsh funnel). Adjust with water or additional Carry Flow before drilling.
